source: All-In Podcast — GPT-5 underwhelms, AI TAM/ROIC/energy, China's advantage, tariffs, Nvidia chip smuggling, Apple buybacks and AI strategy
summary: Deep Seek employees in China are subject to CCP surveillance and isolation from Americans, confirming China views AI as an existential national security competition.
summary_extended: Baker claims, based on what he describes as reliable intelligence, that employees of DeepSeek in China are prohibited from being in the same room as Americans and are accompanied by CCP minders at all times. He presents this as concrete evidence that China views AI development as an existential national security competition, not merely a commercial endeavor. Baker argues this asymmetry matters because the US may not be treating AI with the same strategic urgency, creating a geopolitical risk that investors in AI infrastructure and frontier models should factor into long-term positioning. No specific companies are named as direct subjects or beneficiaries of this thesis; it is a macro geopolitical observation used to frame the broader AI race narrative. The investment implication is diffuse — it supports a long-term bullish view on US AI infrastructure and defense-adjacent AI spending, but Baker does not translate it into a specific actionable trade in this segment.
detail: Baker states he has it 'on good authority' that Deep Seek employees are not allowed to be in the same room as Americans while in China and have CCP minders with them most of the time. He uses this as evidence that China treats AI as an existential competition, regardless of whether the US does.
confidence_evidence: Baker cites a specific intelligence-type claim ('on good authority') but it is unverifiable. Framed as a data point supporting a broader thesis rather than a standalone investment call.
quote_fragment: if you work for Deep Seek, you are not allowed to be in the same room as an American
